I've now viewed 16 reference images. Let me analyze the findings:

- Two corn ears with husks pulled back
- Entire ear surface covered uniformly with blue-gray/grayish-blue powdery mold

**Class comparison:**
- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot** (seed/26): Dark blue-green mold growing between yellow kernels — closest color and pattern match; KB description says "dark blue-green layers of conidia...covering all kernels from base to middle"
- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**: Olive-green (not blue-gray), more localized at tip — no match
- **Diplodia_Ear_Rot**: White mycelium, grayish-brown mummified ears — no match
- **Gibberella_Disease**: Pink/red mold at ear tip — no match
- **Head_Smut**: Dark brown spore mass replacing ear structure — no match
- **Common_Smut**: Large white-to-silver galls — no match
- **Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight**: Dark mold at husk tips — no match
- **Fusarium_Disease**: Whitish-pink mold patches — no match

The heavy, uniform blue-gray-green mold covering the entire ear surface best matches Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, which specifically describes "dark blue-green layers of conidia on and between kernels...covering all kernels and husk leaf layers."
